assessments.reasoning: N4950 module.unit paragraph 2 defines an interface unit through an export-led declaration and requires exactly one interface unit without a module partition in each named module. The same sentence designates it primary and makes a diagnostic unnecessary.

challenge.method: Compare a named module's primary interface, its exported interface partition under paragraph 3, an implementation unit, and the global module described on the following page. Check whether the diagnostic exception changes the underlying requirement.
challenge.results: Named modules retain the one-unpartitioned-interface requirement. An exported partition can coexist with that primary interface, and the global module is outside the requirement. The diagnostic clause governs reporting.

limitations: No diagnostic is required for violating this N4950 requirement. The text still imposes the underlying requirement.
